detailed_description:
Photoreal cinematic live-action, 1881 London, 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:04. The shot begins from <Picture 3>: a medium shot on <Subject 1> down on one knee on the dusty boards where Holmes has knelt, bare-headed, sunburnt, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the LEFT half, the tall window flat and grey in the CENTRE of the far wall behind him. The camera is on the boards across the room from Watson, level with his kneeling head and two yards from him, a 50mm lens turned on him and the floor. The tall window stands flat and grey behind him. At the first frame Watson is down on one knee on the dusty boards where Holmes has knelt, bare-headed, sunburnt. The camera pushes a hand's breadth in over the dust as <Subject 1> lowers his head toward the boards, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 his eyes travel along the floor, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. <Subject 1>'s mouth is closed from 00:00 to 00:04 while his bare hand comes down flat beside the marks. By 00:04 the camera has finished pushing a hand's breadth in over the dust and stands at that distance, with the action of that shot completed.
[Shot 2] From 00:04 to 00:07. At 00:04 the shot cuts to an insert straight down on the dusty boards where <Subject 1> is looking, beginning from <Picture 4>: grey dust, the overlapping half-prints of many boots, and one long scuff running away toward the far wall; only what <Picture 4> shows is in frame. The camera is above the boards where Watson is looking, pointing straight down, a forearm above the floor, a 50mm lens turned on the dust. Flat fog-grey light falls across it from the window. At the first frame The stripped floorboards fill the frame under a grey film of dust. The overlapping half-prints of many boots cross and recross the boards, their edges broken and their patterns trodden out of each other. One long scuff runs away toward the far wall, the dust pushed aside along it down to the bare grain. Every print lies broken across another under the grey film. The camera pushes straight in on the trampled boards as the dust lifts a little where a breath crosses it, from 00:04 to 00:07. By 00:07 the camera has finished pushing straight in on the trampled boards and stands at that distance, with the action of that shot completed.
